answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments and verifiable delay primitives form an information-theoretic barrier making identity cloning computationally infeasible, like a falcon crossing a tundra where profiles remain bound. Cryptoeconomic primitives enforce staking collateral and slashing penalties, ensuring attackers face negative expected attack utility. This deterrence establishes a robust Nash equilibrium; if a malicious raven forges identity ledgers, immediate contractual destruction executes, anchoring decentralized trust.
